q: the arolsen cards three german index cards, attached to hedviga's husband in the family tree and never read, place him in a factory in wür  reutlingen and pfullingen, 1941–42 · surveyed 1950 the arolsen cards three german index cards, attached to hedviga's husband in the family tree and never read, place him in a factory in württemberg at the age of sixteen. the media sweep turned up three record images filed under ivan anton defranceski (1925–1995) from the arolsen archives — the international tracing service, the central archive of nazi persecution. the previous build of this archive listed them as an open question because nobody had looked at them. this page is what they say. the identification is firm. all three give the birth as 25 june 1925 at crikvenica — the same day and place as the 1951 yugoslav birth extract , which records the father of hedviga's children as “ivan defranceski, born 25.06.1925, crikvenica”. one of the three cards writes 24 .6.25; that is a clerical slip against two other cards and a civil certificate. what the cards record name defranceski , forename written iwan and jvan — german renderings of ivan born 25 june 1925 , crikvenica — spelled grikvenica and cricvenica by two different clerks nationality kroatien-jugoslawien on one card; ? on another status led. — ledig , single. no wife and no children are entered on the insurance card, and every family line is blank. lodging pfullingen, brunnenstraße 7 ; the reutlingen card gives the unterkunftsort simply as reutlingen employer 1 licht u. kraft , reutlingen — apparently the electricity and power undertaking. category hilfsarb. — hilfsarbeiter , unskilled labourer. 21 october 1941 – 16 january 1942. employer 2 a second reutlingen employer, same category. the name is written in an old german hand and this archive cannot read it confidently — it begins with what may be otto . 26 january 1942 – 28 november 194? — the final digit of the year runs into the column rule and is illegible. it is 1942 or 1944 , and the difference is ten months against nearly three years. insurance registration and deregistration numbers 8143 / 560 for the first post, 905 / 8614 for the second he turned sixteen in june 1941 and started at licht und kraft that october . the most important thing on these cards is what is missing three blank lines the 1950 municipal questionnaires exist precisely to establish what kind of worker a foreigner had been. three printed lines do that job. on both cards, all three are empty. wurde der arbeiter restlos entlohnt? “was the worker paid in full?” — blank dienstverpflichtet compulsorily assigned to service — blank freier arbeiter … seit free worker, since — blank so the record establishes that he was there and what he did , and is silent on the one question everybody asks first. this archive does not claim he was a forced labourer, and does not claim he went voluntarily. the boxes that would settle it were left empty by a german town clerk in 1950, five years after the fact. nor does the file title settle it. the collection is catalogued by the arolsen archives as “card file of persecutees in the later french zone and of french persecutees in other areas” (de its 2.3.3.1). that is the name of a zone-wide registration file compiled by the occupation authorities, not a finding about any individual in it. being in the file is not a finding of persecution. the second collection is the war time card file — registration cards, employees' record books, individual correspondence (02020201 os). the context, stated as context yugoslavia was invaded on 6 april 1941 and partitioned; the independent state of croatia was declared on 10 april 1941 under axis supervision, and sent workers to the reich under labour agreements. german recruitment of labour from the region hardened through late 1941 and 1942 as the war in the east stalled and the demand for workers became acute. ivan's first registration — 21 october 1941 — sits early in that sequence, before the openly coercive round-ups documented from 1942 onward. that is a reason to be careful in both directions: it does not make his going voluntary, and it does not make it forced. a sixteen-year-old from an occupied country working in a german power undertaking is not a free labour market in any case. reutlingen and pfullingen are neighbouring towns in württemberg. after 1945 they fell inside württemberg-hohenzollern , the french occupation zone administered from tübingen — which is why a croatian teenager's wartime employment was surveyed by french-zone municipalities in 1950 and why the insurance card is stamped document exploité . the cards krankenkasse membership and benefits card (mitglieder- und leistungskarte nr. 1), printed in fraktur. stamped diagonally document exploité by the french occupation authority. municipal questionnaire, reutlingen, kreis reutlingen, land württemberg — dated to 1950 with the annotation a.o.k. municipal questionnaire, stadt pfullingen, kreis reutlingen, württemberg-hohenzollern — stamped and signed 28 february 1950. where it sits in the life this is the earliest documented event in ivan defranceski's life after his birth, and it reframes the man hedviga married. 25 june 1925 born at crikvenica 21 oct 1941 aged 16 — begins at licht und kraft, reutlingen, as an unskilled labourer, lodging at brunnenstraße 7, pfullingen 26 jan 1942 – 28 nov 194? a second reutlingen employer 1948 back in croatia: his daughter ladislava is born at crikvenica 17 dec 1951 his son ivan born at senj hospital; the birth extract gives his trade as electro-mechanic — which is what a boy who spent the war in a power undertaking might well become — and his nationality as italian 1954 that extract is drawn and translated for the supreme court of south africa 30 oct 1995 dies at senj. hedviga dies at johannesburg on the same date, six years later. what would settle the rest. the arolsen archives online collections hold these cards and may hold more under the same name — a direct search for defranceski, born 25.6.1925 would show the full file and resolve the illegible year. arolsen answers q: blažević the name the archive carries. eight generations, from a boy born about 1750 in a bunjevac settlement to a woman who died  smokvica krmpotska, then senj blažević the name the archive carries. eight generations, from a boy born about 1750 in a bunjevac settlement to a woman who died in johannesburg. 220 published people 1750 earliest birth year 4 distinct spellings in the tree where they are from every blažević ancestor on the direct line before 1892 is placed at smokvica krmpotska , a village in the vinodol hills behind novi vinodolski — founded, like krivi put, by bunjevci krmpoćani settled there by the military frontier between 1605 and 1647. the settlement → the move to town toma blažević (1838–1907) is the hinge. he is born at house 114 in smokvica krmpotska and he dies at senj , a nadničar — day labourer. the family comes off the mountain into a port town in the decades after that port stopped working. senj → his death entry, read the senj death register for 1907 (p.225, entry 60) gives him in full: 26 srpnja — july — 1907 , blažević toma, nadničar , udovac iza pok. tereze — widower of the late tereza — aged 69 , of tuberculosis , sacraments administered, buried at the cemetery of sv. vid on 28 july . he is not alone on that page. two entries above him a tobacco-factory worker of thirty dies of the same disease, three days earlier; three entries above, a coachman of twenty-four is entered as ustrieljen — shot — with the sacraments not administered. this is one week in one small town. house 114 is a zadruga the register identifies a household by its house number, and one number runs through this family. toma blažević is born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska in 1838, and is recorded there with terezija pećanić at the baptisms of ivan in 1882 and tonka in 1884 . in 1895 juraj appears in the same book as “jurko blažević i tereza rođ. žubrinić, selj. ” , at smokvica kbr. 114 . this archive first read that as one household, and was wrong. a control document settles it: the baptism of frane blažević, 2 august 1890 , puts pave blažević i marija rođ. tomljanović at smokvica 114 as well — and that pavao is the son of luka , not of toma. three distinct nuclear families share the number across thirteen years. they join one generation up. luka blažević and anton blažević , toma's father, are both sons of ilija blažević . pavao and toma are first cousins . smokvica 114 is therefore a zadruga — the south slav extended-family household, in which married brothers and cousins live under one number and hold the land in common. it is the characteristic form of the military frontier and of the bunjevac settlements . so the number places juraj inside ilija's kin-group , which is real and worth having, and it does not single out which man in that group was his father. what still would → the parish, at last the same entry gives his birthplace not as a village but as a parish : sv. jakov krmpote — st james of krmpote. that is the register that holds smokvica krmpotska, and therefore the book in which juraj , anton , ilija , grgica and mateša should be found. nobody has opened it. open questions → a caution about the surname blažević is the 17th most common surname in croatia — 7,216 bearers there, 11,163 worldwide — and its densest counties are split-dalmatia, virovitica-podravina and osijek-baranja, none of which is this family's. shared surname is not evidence of shared descent here. the names → where they were born 16 mrzli dol, senj, croatia 11 senj, lika-senj county, croatia 10 senj, croatia 9 mrzli krmpotska and krivi put are not ancient. they were settled on purpose, in living memory of the ottoman wars, by refugees the habsburgs planted on an empty mountain to hold it. two of hedviga's four grandparental lines — the blaževići of smokvica krmpotska and the prpići of krivi put — come out of villages in the senj hinterland that did not exist in 1600 . knowing that changes what it means to say the family is “from” there. who the bunjevci are the bunjevci are a catholic south slavic group whose homeland before the ottoman wars lay in the western balkan hinterland, around the krmpote district near zemunik behind zadar. the krmpotić clan — the largest of them — abandoned that territory under ottoman pressure between about 1465 and 1467 , and moved north and toward the coast. they are usually described in three branches: the dalmatian bunjevci, the danubian bunjevci who ended up around subotica in the bačka, and the littoral–lika bunjevci. this family belongs to the third. 1605–1647 the planting of the senj mountain the first organised migration to the croatian littoral is dated to 1605 , when about fifty families from krmpote near zemunik were settled at lič near fužine. further waves down to 1647 settled the hinterland of senj — ledenice, krmpote, krivi put and the senjska draga . the settlers brought the name of the district they had left: the new krmpote in the vinodol hills is named for the old krmpote behind zadar, and smokvica krmpotska — “smokvica of the krmpote people” — carries it in its surname. this was frontier policy, not accident. the habsburg military frontier needed a loyal, armed, catholic population on the empty ground behind senj. the settlers got land and grazing; the empire got a militia. the name of the road. the story told locally is that a bunjevac, asked which way some venetian fugitives had gone, answered that they had taken the crooked path — krivi put — and the district, until then called svetojakovski and then krmpotski , has been krivi put ever since. this archive records it as local tradition , which is what it is. what that means for this family krivi put 136 the prpići are recorded at a specific house: krivi put 136 . thirty-five people in this tree are born at that address, including antonija “tonka” prpić on 12 may 1859 , baptised three days later at krivi put with lucas and anna tomljanović standing as godparents. house numbers are how the frontier registers worked. a settled family is its house number for a century at a time — which is why the same address can produce four generations. smokvica krmpotska, house 114 toma blažević was born on 27 january 1838 at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska — br. for broj , number. his father anton , his grandfather ilija (b. c. 1790) and the two men above them are all placed in the same village. in 1835 krivi put was the seat of a captain's post under krmpote, with 98 houses and 1,246 people . that is the scale of the world these families were born into. how these households actually worked the zadruga at smokvica 114 the registers do not just place this family in a bunjevac village. they show it living in the characteristic household form of the frontier and the settlements — and this archive only saw it after reading a document meant as a control. 1838 toma blažević born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska 1882, 1884 toma and terezija pećanić , seljaci , at smokvica 114 — the baptisms of ivan and tonka 1890 pavao blažević and marija tomljanović at smokvica 114 — and this pavao is the son of luka , not of toma 1895 “jurko blažević i tereza rođ. žubrinić, selj. ” at smokvica kbr. 114 — the baptism of marijan 1912 antonija's marriage names her parents as “†† toma i tereza blažević, poljodjelci iz sela smokvica kbr. 114” luka and anton — toma's father — are both sons of ilija blažević , born about 1790. so pavao and toma are first cousins , and three generations of ilija's descendants share one house number. that is a zadruga : the south slav extended-family household, in which married brothers and cousins live under one roof and one number and hold the land in common. it was the ordinary form of tenure in the military frontier , where a household — not a man — owed the regiment its service, and it survived in these settlements long after the frontier itself was abolished in 1881. what it cost this archive. the house number was read here as a household, and used as strong evidence that toma was juraj's father. it is not. it identifies a kin-group , and cannot say which man in it was whose father. what still could → and why it is invisible ten miles away the town does not count houses the village registers of krmpote and krivi put enter a house number against every child — smokvica 114 , krivi put 136 , klenovica 22 , povile 22 . the town register of senj does not. under the same printed column — mjesto obitavanja i kućni broj , place of residence and house number — a senj entry says simply “senj” . so the papići cannot be traced through a house the way the blaževići can, and a zadruga among them would be invisible even if it existed . that is a difference between a town and a village, not between two families — and it is worth knowing before concluding anything from the absence. the bunjevac identity is asserted here by place, not by document. no record in this tree calls anyone a bunjevac. what the records give is birth in villages that were founded by bunjevci and populated by them, bearing surnames — blažević, prpić, tomljanović, vukelić — that are standard in those settlements. that is a q: what changed an archive that never contradicts itself is not being careful; it is not checking. this is the list of claims made here   twenty-one things this archive got wrong, and what fixed them what changed an archive that never contradicts itself is not being careful; it is not checking. this is the list of claims made here and then withdrawn, kept in the open because the reasoning that failed is as useful as the reasoning that held. every page here carries a confidence label, and a label is only honest if it can be lowered . most of what follows is this archive becoming less certain, not more: a house number demoted from an identifier to a kin-group, a resolved name reopened, a culprit un-named. one was caught by the reader — the search had been folding surnames and not given names, and was finding 42 of 88 ivans. one was caught by sweeping the built site rather than the source, which is a lesson about where to look. 13 september 2026 1. šojat is a family. i called it a by-name. this archive said recorded in the register as the by-name the tree attaches to one blažević household — read as a nadimak , like papa on the antići. the record says the šojati are a krivi put family of fifteen people with their own dates and their own place — marko šojat, 19 april 1801 to 4 february 1871, five dated children, and a valley called sojat dol . they married the blaževići and prpići nine times . what it cost the mechanism was right and the direction was backwards. blažević (sojat) is almost certainly a household known by the family it married — which is how a nadimak is born, not what one is. who they married → where it now stands → 13 september 2026 2. a bracket and a slash cost this archive 214 people. this archive said that the tree held 232 žubrinići in 94 pieces , and that joining them was the largest single piece of work outstanding in this archive . the record says the surname fold split on ( but not on / . so žubrinić / xubrinich and prpic perpic — one surname written several ways in a single field — never matched the surname list. the real figure is 422 , and fixing it brought 214 people into the archive, including elias ilija žubrinić and casparus žubrinić , who are the subjects of two of this archive's own open questions. what it cost two published numbers, and the conclusion drawn from them. counted properly there are 90 loose ends, not 94 — and 79 of them are bare names with no date and no place. so the work is not large ; it is impossible from here , and the register is the only way through. the fragments, counted → where it now stands → 13 september 2026 3. ninety-two žubrinići were held together by an alphabet. this archive said nothing — this had never been noticed. the tree looked more joined than it is. the record says eighteen nodes whose entire given name is a single letter — m , j , t — each with a parent called “žubrinić zubrinix xubrinic zub” and each holding as children everyone whose name starts with that letter. one has 26 children . what it cost 92 people are attached to the letter their name begins with and to nothing else. the sorting-bucket filter missed them because a bucket is normally detected by words like to be sorted , and these are named a through w. read as parentage — which is what a naive count does — it makes the žubrinići look like a family. where it now stands → september 2026 4. house 114 was called a household. it is a zadruga. this archive said that smokvica krmpotska kbr. 114 identified one family, and so placed juraj blažević in toma's household — nearly naming toma are first cousins and the number covers an extended-family compound — a zadruga . what it cost question 1b was downgraded from critical to substantive. the house places juraj in ilija's kin-group; it cannot name his father. where it now stands → september 2026 5. zvonimir vukelić was not a casualty-list death. this archive said that he should be looked for in the austro-hungarian verlustlisten , reasoning from his age — thirty-two in the second year of the war. the record says the tree places his death at senj and gives his occupation as gostioničar, bankar . a man who dies at home in a settled trade is not a casualty-list entry. what it cost the right book is the senj death register for 1915 . the reasoning was plausible and it was still wrong: an age is not a cause. where arrives through matija pilipić , ahnentafel 13 — the papić line. moved. what it cost nothing to the evidence; everything to whether a reader can follow the line it belongs to. where it now stands → september 2026 7. two letters went to the wrong archive. this archive said both drafted to državni arhiv u gospiću , on the assumption that lika-senj county means gospić. the record says gospić's remit is lika-senj “osim gradova senja i novalje” — except the towns of senj and novalja . and smokvica is in primorje-gorski kotar, not lika-senj at all. both belong to rijeka, senj branch . what it entered joannes , joannis , juan or ive . 268 canonical given names, 34 of them under more than one spelling. what it cost caught by the reader, not by this archive. both surnames and given names now fold — and the split by sex was a second correction on top, after franjo and franciska were wrongly merged. where it now stands → september 2026 9. forty latin case-endings were blamed on a who they married a pedigree takes one person per generation and drops the rest. look instead at who a family marries repeatedly and different things appear: a german name inside the military frontier, a krivi put family that married the blaževići nine times, six marriages into one otočac household, and an adoption working its way through three generations of surnames. correction, 13 september 2026 are a krivi put family with fifteen people, dates and a place of their own . marko šojat, born 19 april 1801 at krivi put, died 4 february 1871 , with five children whose births and deaths are all recorded — šimun 1819, marija 1825, matija 1828, mate 1830, martin 1831. one of them is entered at a place called sojat dol 54 — a valley named after the family. and they married the blaževići nine times. marija šojat 1825–1896 m. anton “kljapo” blažević · 9 children kate sojat b. 1844 m. joso blažević marija sojat m. antona blažević · 4 children mare sojat m. antone blažević · 2 children marija sojat m. mile blažević nikola šojat b. 1878 m. kata blažević maria sojath 1823–1891 m. domianus perpić · 4 children ivka sojat m. dametar perpić ivan sojat m. ivka prpić so blažević (sojat) in the tree is almost certainly a household known by the family it married — which is how a nadimak is born, and the opposite of what this archive said. the mechanism was right and the direction was backwards. untersinger — a german name inside the frontier seven people, and unusually for this archive they are a complete three-generation household with dates : lucas untersinger → george, born 25 march 1787, died 1848 , married to helena → five children, rosalia 1802, ana 1807–1845 , michael 1810–1840, lucia 1827, eva 1839. ana untersinger married elias “ilija” žubrinić , and they both died in 1845 , leaving seven children — the event question 4b suspects was an epidemic in lika. a german surname in lika is not an accident. the military frontier was administered from vienna and its officer, forestry and clerical grades were staffed from across the monarchy. a žubrinić marrying an untersinger in the 1820s is a frontier family marrying into the administration of the frontier — which fits the six salaried posts this family held. what would test it: the otočac registers for george untersinger (1787) and his father lucas, and whether either is entered with a rank or an office. if the untersingers arrived as frontier staff rather than as settlers, the entry will say so. but the household does not hold together checked against itself on 13 september 2026, this “complete three-generation household” contradicts itself twice. george is born in 1787 and rosalia in 1802 — he would be fifteen. and helena is born in june 1788 and eva in 1839 , making her fifty-one. neither is impossible; both together, in a family of seven, are a warning. the likeliest reading is that rosalia and eva are not george and helena's children at all — that a generation is compressed, as it is in several other households here . which matters for the argument above, because the dates are the only reason to place the marriage “in the 1820s”. not one untersinger is published on this site — which is why nobody looked at the household as a household. to be exact about it, one of the two was already caught: helena bearing eva at fifty-one is on the contradictions page as a mother-too-old. the other, george at fifteen, sits just under that check's threshold of thirteen and was never flagged at all. added 13 september 2026 butorac — a household that stood godparent twice and is not in the tree reading the godparent column for the first time turned up jandre and marija butorac standing for two of toma blažević's children at smokvica 114 — ivan in 1882 and tonka in 1884 . the 1882 entry names her explicitly as “marija butorac, supruga jandrina” , jandre's wife. standing twice, two years apart, is not a courtesy. it is a standing relationship between two households , and it is the kind of tie that marriage records and house numbers usually hide. neither of them is in this tree. the only butorac in the entire export is margareta butorac , born 4 march 1870 at ledenice, who married franjo kalanj — a different family, a different village, and too young to be either godparent. so jandre and marija are known to this archive from one column of one register and from nowhere else. what would test it: the sv. jakov krmpote marriage register for a jandre butorac, and the house number his household is entered under. if it is near 114, the tie is neighbourhood; if it is far, it is more likely kin — and the mother of these children is a pećanić , whose own people are barely in this archive either. added 13 september 2026 katnić — seventeen people at crikvenica, none published seventeen katnići sit in the export, running 1722 to 1950 , and almost all of them at crikvenica — which is where ana kalanj's grave is, and where the defranceski side of hedviga's household buried its dead. none is published here, because katnić is not one of the nine surnames. they surface only as a contradiction: luka katnić , born 1722 and died 10 december 1755 , is entered as the father of margaretha (1757) and magdalena (1768) — thirteen years after his death. that is one of the twenty , and it is a wrong join rather than a bad date. noted rather than pursued. they belong to the crikvenica material, which is mostly the sister archive's, and this page exists to say where the edges of this one are. kostelac — six marriages into one household fifteen people, and six of them married žubrinići : stephanus married barbara žubrinić; maria kostelacz, juliana kostelacz and maria kostelac each married a joannes žubrinić; martinus married francisca žubrinić; michaël married lucia žubrinić. a seventh, mande kostelac, married a sekula . two consequences. three women of one surname married men of one name — which is exactly the soil in which the michaël žubrinić confusion grew, and a warning about how little a name identifies here. and one couple is in the tree twice. stephanus kostelacz + barbara žubrinić and stipan kostelac + bare žubrinić are the same marriage under latin and croatian forms of both names — and both versions carry a daughter born 19 april 1849 , entered once as lucia and once as luce . orešković and sekula — an adoption, and why question 4d was hard the 1835 otočac baptism of maria catharina enters her father as marcus oreskovich, adoptatus sekula . the tree explains it: marcus orešković, born 18 april 1809, is the son of vitus sekula . he was born a sekula and carries orešković. then he married a sekula — lucia, born 14 april 1815, daughter of a different sekula household — and two of their sons carry both surnames at once : franciscus orešković oreskovic sekula (1844) and petrus orešković oreskovic sekula (1846). born one name, living under another, married back into the first, and passing both to his children. that is the same machine as antich papa becoming papić — a surname changing hands over three generations — running in a different family at the same time. the names → and it explains why question 4d was so hard. the žubrinići married oreškovići at least four times : magdalena orešković (b. 1796) married nicolaus žubrinić; francisca (b. 1815) married paulus žubrinić; maria catharina (b. 1835) is given to michael; antonius orešković married helena žubrinić. “a maria orešković married to a michaël žubrinić” was never going to identify anybody — the two families had been marrying each other for half a century. question 4d → kosina — a slovenian merchant who walked over the mountains the family anka blažević married into in 1919, and the family that lost pavao in the 1943 raid , are not croatian. their senj marriage of 12 january 1888 gives martin kosina's origin as kranjska, župa sv. martin kod krainburg — carniola, the parish of st martin near kranj , in what is now slovenia . he was a trgovac , a merchant, and 47 when he married the 30-year-old angjelika boras , a šilica — seamstress. the entry names only his mother , gertruda kosina, posjednica — a woman of property, with a german name and no husband recorded. two generations later the family was senj's. martin's sons pavao and antun married four days apart in november 1919, both entered trgovac like their father; pavao was killed in the air raid of 8 october 1943; and the grave that carries him was restored by the family in 1991 with a priest's cross against it. senj, 1943 → the boras side held office: josip boras, gradski stražar — city guard — and the witness ivan boras, kr. pomorske straže nadstražar , senior officer of the royal maritime guard. what these families have in common none of them is on the direct line. all four change what the direct line means . repetition is the signal. nine šojat marriages, six kostelac, four orešković. a single marriage tells you two people met; nine tells you two villages were one community. names move between families. šojat becomes a blažević by-name; sekula becomes an orešković surname and then both; papa becomes papić. three separate instances of one mechanism , and this archive has now caught all three. and it is why identification keeps failing. when four oreškovići marry four žubrinići, a name and a surname identify nothing at all. what cannot be true →  who they the six salaried posts this family held. what would test it: the otocac registers for george untersinger (1787) and his father lucas, and whether either is entered with a rank or an office. if the untersingers arrived as frontier staff rather than as settlers, the entry will say so. but the household does not hold together checked against itself on 13 september 2026, this “complete three-generation household” contradicts itself twice. george is born in 1787 and rosalia in 1802 — he would be fifteen. and helena is born in june 1788 and eva in 1839 , making her fifty-one. neither is impossible; both together, in a family of seven, are a warning. the likeliest reading is that rosalia and eva are not george and helena's children at all — that a generation is compressed, as it is in several other households here . which matters for the argument above, because the dates are the only reason to place the marriage “in the 1820s”. not one untersinger is published on this site — which is why nobody looked at the household as a household. to be exact about it, one of the two was already caught: helena bearing eva at fifty-one is on the contradictions page as a mother-too-old. the other, george at fifteen, sits just under that check's threshold of thirteen and was never flagged at all. added 13 september 2026 butorac — a household that stood godparent twice and is not in the tree reading the godparent column for the first time turned up jandre and marija butorac standing for two of toma blazevic's children at smokvica 114 — ivan in 1882 and tonka in 1884 . the 1882 entry names her explicitly as “marija butorac, supruga jandrina” , jandre's wife. standing twice, two years apart, is not a courtesy. it is a standing relationship between two households , and it is the kind of tie that marriage records and house numbers usually hide. neither of them is in this tree. the only butorac in the entire export is margareta butorac , born 4 march 1870 at ledenice, who married franjo kalanj — a different family, a different village, and too young to be either godparent. so jandre and marija are known to this archive from one column of one register and from nowhere else. what would test it: the sv. jakov krmpote marriage register for a jandre butorac, and the house number his household is entered under. if it is near 114, the tie is neighbourhood; if it is far, it is more likely kin — and the mother of these children is a pecanic , whose own people are barely in this archive either. added 13 september 2026 katnic — seventeen people at crikvenica, none published seventeen katnici sit in the export, running 1722 to 1950 , and almost all of them at crikvenica — which is where ana kalanj's grave is, and where the defranceski side of hedviga's household buried its dead. none is published here, because katnic is not one of the nine surnames. they surface only as a contradiction: luka katnic , born 1722 and died 10 december 1755 , is entered as the father of margaretha (1757) and magdalena (1768) — thirteen years after his death. that is one of the twenty , and it is a wrong join rather than a bad date. noted rather than pursued. they belong to the crikvenica material, which is mostly the sister archive's, and this page exists to say where the edges of this one are. kostelac — six marriages into one household fifteen people, and six of them married zubrinici : stephanus married barbara zubrinic; maria kostelacz, juliana kostelacz and maria kostelac each married a joannes zubrinic; martinus married francisca zubrinic; michael married lucia zubrinic. a seventh, mande kostelac, married a sekula . two consequences. three women of one surname married men of one name — which is exactly the soil in which the michael zubrinic confusion grew, and a warning about how little a name identifies here. and one couple is in the tree twice. stephanus kostelacz + barbara zubrinic and stipan kostelac + bare zubrinic are the same marriage under latin and croatian forms of both names — and both versions carry a daughter born 19 april 1849 , entered once as lucia and once as luce . oreskovic and sekula — an adoption, and why question 4d was hard the 1835 otocac baptism of maria catharina enters her father as marcus oreskovich, adoptatus sekula . the tree explains it: marcus oreskovic, born 18 april 1809, is the son of vitus sekula . he was born a sekula and carries oreskovic. then he married a sekula — lucia, born 14 april 1815, daughter of a different sekula household — and two of their sons carry both surnames at once : franciscus oreskovic oreskovic sekula (1844) and petrus oreskovic oreskovic sekula (1846). born one name, living under another, married back into the first, and passing both to his children. that is the same machine as antich papa becoming papic — a surname changing hands over three generations — running in a different family at the same time. the names → and it explains why question 4d was so hard. the zubrinici married oreskovici at least four times : magdalena oreskovic (b. 1796) married nicolaus zubrinic; francisca (b. 1815) married paulus zubrinic; maria catharina (b. 1835) is given to michael; antonius oreskovic married helena zubrinic. “a maria oreskovic married to a michael zubrinic” was never going to identify anybody — the two families had been marrying each other for half a century. question 4d → kosina — a slovenian merchant who walked over the mountains the family anka blazevic married into in 1919, and the family that lost pavao in the 1943 raid , are not croatian. their senj marriage of 12 january 1888 gives martin kosina's origin as kranjska, zupa sv. martin kod krainburg — carniola, the parish of st martin near kranj , in what is now slovenia . he was a trgovac , a merchant, and 47 when he married the 30-year-old angjelika boras , a silica — seamstress. the entry names only his mother , gertruda kosina, posjednica — a woman of property, with a german name and no husband recorded. two generations later the family was senj's. martin's sons pavao and antun married four days apart in november 1919, both entered trgovac like their father; pavao was killed in the air raid of 8 october 1943; and the grave that carries him was restored by the family in 1991 with a priest's cross against it. senj, 1943 → the boras side held office: josip boras, gradski strazar — city guard — and the witness ivan boras, kr. pomorske straze nadstrazar , senior officer of the royal maritime guard. what these families have in common none of them is on the direct line. all four change what the direct line means . repetition is the signal. nine sojat marriages, six kostelac, four oreskovic. a single marriage tells you two people met; nine tells you two villages were one community. names move between families. sojat becomes a blazevic by-name; sekula becomes an oreskovic surname and then both; papa becomes papic. three separate instances of one mechanism , and this archive has now caught all three. and it is why identification keeps failing. when four oreskovici marry four zubrinici, a name and a surname identify nothing at all. what cannot be true →

q: the same person, twice a duplicate is not a mystery to be solved. it is one person counted as two, and it quietly inflates every number this ar  19 duplicates confirmed, 32 rejected the same person, twice a duplicate is not a mystery to be solved. it is one person counted as two, and it quietly inflates every number this archive publishes about itself. finding them is easy. not over-finding them turned out to be the hard part. this check began as a žubrinić-only test and that was the mistake. run across all 1245 published people it finds the same disease in four families — and the first version of it was badly wrong , in a way worth showing rather than quietly fixing. what the first run claimed, and why it was wrong matching on surname, given name and birth year, the tool reported 42 duplicate groups holding 47 surplus records . that number is nonsense. most of those pairs are two different people who share a name — which is the one error this archive has warned about on every other page, since it holds eighteen ivan blaževići and refuses to auto-link names anywhere for exactly that reason. having written the warning, i walked into it. two tests fixed it. different parents means different people. nicolaus žubrinić, born at otočac in 1834, is the son of michael in one record and of lucas in the other — and he is ahnentafel 10 , a direct ancestor. without that test this page would have announced that this archive's own great-great-grandfather was a duplicate. and two death years means two people : antonius kalanj of klenovica 22, born 1868, is entered as dying in 1868 and in 1873. that is not one boy twice. it is a necronym — a dead child's name given to the next baby, which these families did constantly. with both tests the count falls from 42. the refinements below then bring it back up to 19 , because a test that is too strict throws away real duplicates as surely as a loose one invents them. comparing names is harder than it looks three further corrections were needed, and two of them came from outside the data — one from a photograph of a grave, one from noticing what was in the father's slot. the problem the case the rule a nickname in one record and not the other marijan cigo kalanj and marijan kalanj match given names by containment , not equality parents' names spelled differently michael vs michaelis / michael / miho compare parent names as sets, asking whether they overlap a sorting label standing in the father's slot jure žubrinić vs brothers of casparus (it seems) ignore bucket parents entirely — a label is not a father two spellings of one name, disjoint as tokens kate vs katalyn zubrinich where the full birth date, birth place and both parents agree, a shared three-letter prefix is enough a whole family duplicated in parallel lovro and lovre kalanj, each with their own ana, ivan and marijan allow one character of difference in a parent's name and one was forced by a south australian birth index. this archive held kate zubrinich and katalyn zubrinich as two women — identical in birth date, birth place, death date, death place and both parents — and this check walked straight past them, because “kate” and “katalyn” are disjoint tokens rather than one inside the other. a findmypast search of the south australian births settled it: one registration in 1886, at port pirie, for a kate , and no katalyn anywhere in 176 records of that surname. one woman. the last of those was forced by a gravestone . a photograph of a grave at klenovica names lovro kalanj 1906–1965, ana kalanj 1919–1971, ivan kalanj 1942–1996, marijan kalanj 1944–2009 — one family, four people. the tree holds all four twice , and because the duplicated parents are spelled lovro in one copy and lovre in the other, the parent test rejected the children as different people. the stone said otherwise and the stone was right. which is the useful lesson: a parent-agreement test fails precisely when the parents are themselves duplicated. it is a good test and it is not a complete one. what survives the tests by confidence same day 7 same year and place 7 same year only 5 rejected 32 by family zubrinic 10 sheet meant to be shown to somebody in the family. every picture here is attached to a name in the tree — but the caption underneath it is a camera filename or a hedge, so the name is somebody's recollection rather than a record. one afternoon with a relative would close most of this page. this is the one open question in the archive that no archive can answer . a parish register will eventually give up a birth date; nothing in rijeka or gospić will ever say which of two women in a photograph is milka. the people who could say are alive, and the pictures have never been put in plot — and one of them belongs to a man who is not buried in it. two further graves, found since, say something consistent about what a stone is good for and what it is not. the blažević plot, senj. neighbouring stones read vukelić, tomljanović, bezjak and rogić — the same surnames that fill this tree. what is cut into it upper stone ljubomir blažević ✳ 1891 † 1966 milka blažević rod. papić ✳ 1886 † 1971 oto blažević ✳ 1923 † 1945 mario blažević ✳ 1933 † 1984 later plaque blažević — kata ✳ 1924 † 2007 · leo ✳ 1920 † 2008 rod. — rođena , “born”, the croatian equivalent of née . the stone therefore records milka's maiden name, papić — and not the vukelić name she married under in 1920 . why this photograph matters more than any other here it corroborates the account of oto's death oto blažević ✳ 1923 † 1945 is on this stone. the family record carries two irreconcilable accounts of how he died — a snakebite, and the war in slavonia — and the second one, from nives blažević , said this: …he died in the war somewhere in slavonia, his grave is unknown, so they put his name in his grandmother's and grandfather's grave — and now leo is there, and katica . the stone shows exactly that . oto's name is on the family plot; and the later plaque below carries leo (1920–2008) and kata — katica — (1924–2007), added afterwards, precisely as she described. one wrinkle resolves easily. nives calls it “his grandmother's and grandfather's grave”, but the names on it are oto's parents . nives blažević was born in 1953 : ljubomir and milka were her grandparents. she is describing the grave from her own position in the family, which is what people do. what this does and does not prove. it does not prove he died in slavonia. it proves that the person who said so knew this grave in detail — including who was added to it half a century later — and that the family commemorated oto somewhere other than a grave of his own. that is real corroboration of the witness, and it moves the snakebite account into second place. the brother → and it contradicts the register the stone gives ljubomir's birth as 1891 . the 1920 marriage register , written in his lifetime from his baptismal certificate, gives 1 march 1892 . this archive follows the register. it is a useful reminder in a family whose evidence is mostly stone and memory: a gravestone is a secondary source . it is cut after the fact, paid for by the bereaved, and carved by someone who never met the person. added 13 september 2026 two more graves, and the same lesson twice when that last paragraph was written it rested on one stone. sweeping the family's photo library turned up two more, in two more cemeteries — and one of them repeats the error exactly, while the other corrects the tree. crikvenica. ana de. franceschi marijan kalanj 1944–2009 — a father, a mother and two sons. crikvenica gets a birth date wrong, exactly as senj does the stone gives ana de franceschi, born 19 september 1863 . her baptism survives and does not agree: anno domini 1864 , no. 2 — anna, legitima, josephus kalanj et rosalia nata perković ejus uxor , at klenovica n° 22 , born 3 january 1864 and baptised three days later. the death on the stone, 28 may 1936, is exactly right; the birth is out by three and a half months. so both stones this archive can test get the birth wrong and the death right — which makes sense. the death is what the family had just lived through. the birth is what somebody remembered, seventy years later. every name on the crikvenica stone is in the tree read against the record it resolves into one q: hedviga hedviga “seka” blažević was born in a dying port on the adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the highveld, havi  senj 1926 — johannesburg 2001 hedviga hedviga “seka” blažević was born in a dying port on the adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the highveld, having crossed a world war, a country that stopped existing, and two continents. she is the reason this archive exists, and she is also its best-documented person: a birth at senj on 3 august 1926 , a marriage into the defranceski family, three children, an immigration from zimbabwe in april 1975 , a second marriage to a sephardic jew from rhodes, and a death at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 with the cause written down plainly. what the record gives born 3 august 1926, senj father ljubomir “ljubo” blažević (1892–1966), mornar — sailor mother milka lucia papić (1886–1971) — tobacco-factory worker at twenty-one, widow at twenty-eight, supervisor by the end siblings leo (1920–2008), karmela “carmen” (1922–1987), oto (1923–1945) , ljubomir (1929–2007), mario (1933–1984), anton half-siblings by her mother's first marriage: miroslava “mica” vukelić (1907–1993) and josip vukelić (1913–2004). milka's two marriages → married ivan anton defranceski (1925–1995) — who spent part of the war as a sixteen-year-old labourer in a german power works. the arolsen cards → children ladislava “ada” (b. 1948, crikvenica), ivan anton (b. 1951, senj), robert “robbie” (b. 1953, senj) emigrated april 1975, to south africa from zimbabwe later married santou (shemtov) isaac codron (1913–1997), born on rhodes — c. 1973, south africa died 30 october 2001, johannesburg, aged 75 cause cancer of the rectum, spread to the liver the shape of the life she was born into a household of seven children in a town whose economy had already collapsed — the railway had bypassed senj half a century before she was born. her mother supervised women rolling cigarettes; her father went to sea. she was fifteen when the independent state of croatia was declared and the war reached the coast, and nineteen when it ended and her brother oto did not come home. her first two children were born in yugoslavia , at crikvenica and senj. then africa — and it is worth being exact about the order, because the record is: she was in zimbabwe first , and came south to south africa in april 1975 . she is described as having married codron around 1973 , which places that marriage in the rhodesian years, not the south african ones. family lore, recorded september 2026 twenty-two years this archive cannot account for the record has her at senj in april 1953 , when robert was born, and in south africa in april 1975 , arriving from zimbabwe. between those two dates there is nothing at all — twenty-two years, an emigration, and an entire country she is only known to have been in because of the words “from zimbabwe” on the later entry. three things are remembered in the family about that crossing. they are set down here as what is said , beside what the record holds, and the two do not entirely agree. “they went in 1948” family lore remembered as the year ivan and hedviga left. the record does not allow it. their second and third children were born at senj in december 1951 and april 1953 . the family was in croatia for at least five years after 1948. but 1948 is a real year in this family , and it may be what the memory is anchored to: ladislava “ada” was born at crikvenica on 5 march 1948 . a date attaching itself to the wrong event is the commonest thing in this archive — it is how a man came to be born after his own granddaughter . why they went family lore a post-war migration , for better and safer conditions. nothing in the record speaks to motive at all — not a single document here says why anyone left. what the record does supply is the setting: a town whose economy had collapsed seventy years earlier, a brother dead in 1945 with no grave, and a husband who had spent the war from the age of sixteen as a labourer in a german power works . she sang at the hotel therapia family lore remembered as a singer at the hotel therapia in crikvenica — her husband's home town, and where their first child was born in 1948. the tree records no occupation for her whatsoever. her entire event list is three lines: born, immigrated, died. set against her mother — entered nadglednica u tvornici duhana , a supervisor in the tobacco factory — and her grandmother, a nadničarka , that silence is its own kind of record. this is the only thing anyone has ever said about what hedviga did. and the venue is checkable, which lore rarely is. the therapia opened in 1895 as the nadvojvoda josip — archduke joseph — with 120 beds, and was renamed hotel therapia in 1899 when a hydropathic institute was established inside it. with the miramare of 1906 it is the building that turned crikvenica from a village into an austro-hungarian health resort . a woman singing there was singing in the grandest room on that stretch of coast. “i believe it closed down” corrected it did not. the building stands and is still a hotel. it was bought in 2013 by the austrian hotelier wilfried holleis , renovated, and renamed kvarner palace — four stars, 92 rooms. what closed was the name , not the house. which means the room she is remembered singing in is still there and can be walked into , and that is a rarer thing than a document. why this is written down rather than checked. a migration leaves paper — a passenger list, a permit, a naturalisation file, a school enrolment for three children. none of it has been looked for , because until now this archive did not know there was a rhodesian decade to look in. what would find it → two dates that fall on the same day 30 october her husband ivan anton defranceski died at senj on 30 october 1995 . hedviga died at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 — six years later, to the day. this archive records the coincidence and claims nothing by it. both dates cannot be true no register was needed for any of these. they are dates in one record that cannot all be true at once — a mother who died before her children were born, a woman married eight years after her own death. checking a tree against itself is the cheapest research there is, and it had never been done here. this page exists because of tereza pećanić . she is a direct ancestor, and this archive published her as having died before 1850 — while the same record married her in 1858 and gave her children until 1884 . nothing external was needed to see it. her own page contradicted itself, and it had done so for as long as the site existed. so tools/consistency.py now reads every person in this archive against themselves and against their own family: births after deaths, marriages before births, parents younger than their children. it finds 71 . by how bad impossible 33 very doubtful 23 worth a look 15 impossible means the dates are firm and still conflict. very doubtful means one of them is hedged — abt , bef — so the conflict may be an artefact of the hedge. by kind a child born after the parent died 25 a parent under thirteen 16 a child born before the parent 10 a parent aged thirteen to sixteen 8 a mother over fifty 6 died before being born 1 two generations in too few years 1 married before being born 1 married after dying 1 married as a child 1 lived past a hundred and five 1 added 13 september 2026 sixty-three rows are not sixty-three mistakes every row above is a symptom . one wrong parent link reports once per child, so the page was counting its own consequences — and worse, it was listing four quite different things as though they were one. grouping by pivot person and by cause, the 71 rows collapse to 45 distinct mistakes. kind of mistake causes rows what it means a contradiction in the record 27 40 the dates as written cannot both be true. this is the only kind that is really a finding about the past rather than about the tree. a wrong link 4 8 too far apart for any slop in the dates. the join is wrong, not the dates — usually a reused name, or two people merged. a generation skipped 9 14 the parent is barely older than the s: An evidence-first archive for the family of Hedviga Blažević of Senj.
q: the blažević archive an evidence-first archive for the family of hedviga blažević of senj.  senj · smokvica krmpotska · otočac · krivi put · selce · karlobag one woman, four families, and the mountain they were planted on. an evidence-first archive for hedviga “seka” blažević — born at senj in 1926, dead at johannesburg in 2001 — and for the blaževići, žubrinići, papići and prpići who made her. illustration, not a photograph: a generated image of the northern adriatic coast, standing for senj under the velebit. every document reproduced on this site is the real scan. why the distinction is laboured here → this archive begins with one woman — hedviga “seka” blažević , born at senj on 3 august 1926 , married to ivan anton defranceski, and dead at johannesburg on 30 october 2001 — and works outward into the four families that made her: the blaževići of smokvica krmpotska, the žubrinići of otočac, the papići of senj and selce, and the prpići of krivi put. it reaches nine generations and 70 named ancestors , the earliest born about 1717 . everything here is either sourced, reasoned in the open, or labelled as something the family says and the record does not yet confirm. start with hedviga the spine, nine generations what is still unproven what this archive says they are bunjevci, and that is not a small detail smokvica krmpotska and krivi put were not old croatian q: kalanj the best-placed family in this archive — 87% of its records name a place — and the one whose house has just been seen wh  klenovica and povile kalanj the best-placed family in this archive — 87% of its records name a place — and the one whose house has just been seen whole for the first time. 215 published people 1734 earliest birth year 3 distinct spellings in the tree one house, under two names eighty-five published kalanji carry a klenovica or povile house number, and every one of those houses is entirely kalanj — not one is shared with another surname. the two largest looked separate and are not. petrus kalanj and magdalena butković's ten children are entered povile 22, klenovica 22, klenovica 22, povile 22 , then four at klenovica 22, then two more at povile 22. ivan and josipa alternate the same way across seven children; luka and kata across four. no household moves house nine times and alternates back. povile and klenovica are neighbouring settlements and the registers used the two names for one place. so house 22 holds 67 published people between 1840 and 1890 — the largest single household in the archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136 . the gazetteer → and the smaller numbers are zadrugas too if house 22 is the extended household, the small late numbers ought to be sons splitting off. two of them are not. klenovica 23 (1862–1893) holds the children of four different couples — mate and catharina pa…, josephus and catharina buneta, jandre and manda komadina, joso and manda komadina. klenovica 36 (1892–1894) holds the children of three — luka and kata miletić, joso and manda, franjo and tereza. that is the same signature this archive identified at smokvica 114 : several married couples entered against one number in the same years. so the zadruga is not a smokvica peculiarity or a bunjevac one — it is how klenovica was organised too. houses 37, 38 and 59 hold a single child each and are something else, probably transient. one puzzle sits inside it. luka kalanj and kata miletić have children at house 22, then at 36 in 1892, then at 37 in 1894 — and two of them are called marija . whether that is a family moving twice in two years, a renumbering, or two entries for one child is not answerable from this file. four boys called antonius petrus and magdalena's children include an antonius born in 1865, another in 1868, a third in 1868 and a fourth in 1872. that is not an error. it is a necronym — a dead child's name given to the next born — and it is why the duplicate check has to read two death years as proof of two people rather than evidence of one. how they reach this archive not, as this page used to say, by marrying into the blažević line — that is one marriage, lovro kalanj and klara blažević. the chain that actually carries the family runs through hedviga's husband . ana kalanj , born at klenovica n° 22 on 3 january 1864 and baptised three days later, married josip de franceschi ; their son ante, their grandson pepe. every published kalanj is connected to hedviga by ordinary links — 100% , which only one other family here can say. what that means → four siblings, found loose in a photo library the baptisms of ana (1894), franciska (1896), zora (1898) and ivan (1900) — four consecutive children of martin kalanj and marija peričić at novi vinodolski — were sitting unattached in the family's own photographs. all four match the tree to the day , and the register calls the father martin kalanj josipov , a patronymic that confirms the grandfather independently of the tree. zora's godparents in 1898 are entered josip i ana defrancesco — the child's aunt and uncle , which is how ana's own place in this family was confirmed from a direction nobody was looking in. they are not a klenovica family. they are brinje people. this page, and this whole archive, has treated the kalanji as belonging to klenovica — 119 of them are recorded there. their own baptismal entry says otherwise, and it took an american passenger manifest to make anyone read the line properly. at ana kalanj's baptism, klenovica n° 22, 3 january 1864 , her parents are entered as josephus kalanj et rosalia nata perković ejus uxor, brinjensis parochiae ruricolae — country people of the parish of brinje . brinje is inland , over the kapela, some forty kilometres from the sea. and the tree independently records rozalija perković as being of brinje. so the klenovica kalanji came down to the coast, and every search this archive has run has been on the coast. brinje does not appear in the gazetteer and not one page of its register has been opened. and three of our surnames meet there the emigration records closed the triangle. stipe kalanj , born 1885, sailed for new york in 1910 on la bretagne , gave his residence as brinje , left a wife kate behind, and was met at the dock by his cousin, juro borić . this tree holds a jure borić of brinje — whose daughter ana borić , born 12 february 1885 at brinje, married frane papić of senj , born 27 july 1873. papić is hedviga's mother's family. kalanj, perković and borić are all at brinje, and a borić of brinje married a papić of senj. that is not proof they are one kin-group, and it is not offered as one. it is the observation that the parish where three of this archive's nine surnames overlap is the single parish nobody has ever looked in. what has been searched → and a death nobody can explain martin kalanj died at trebinje on 5 august 1900 , in herzegovina, four hundred kilometres from home — seven months after his youngest child was baptised at novi vinodolski. he was thirty-eight, with five children under seven. military service or work following the garrison are the obvious readings and this archive has evidence for neither. what changed → earliest birth year 3 distinct spellings in the tree one house, under two names eighty-five published kalanji carry a klenovica or povile house number, and every one of those houses is entirely kalanj — not one is shared with another surname. the two largest looked separate and are not. petrus kalanj and magdalena butkovic's ten children are entered povile 22, klenovica 22, klenovica 22, povile 22 , then four at klenovica 22, then two more at povile 22. ivan and josipa alternate the same way across seven children; luka and kata across four. no household moves house nine times and alternates back. povile and klenovica are neighbouring settlements and the registers used the two names for one place. so house 22 holds 67 published people between 1840 and 1890 — the largest single household in the archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136 . the gazetteer → and the smaller numbers are zadrugas too if house 22 is the extended household, the small late numbers ought to be sons splitting off. two of them are not. klenovica 23 (1862–1893) holds the children of four different couples — mate and catharina pa…, josephus and catharina buneta, jandre and manda komadina, joso and manda komadina. klenovica 36 (1892–1894) holds the children of three — luka and kata miletic, joso and manda, franjo and tereza. that is the same signature this archive identified at smokvica 114 : several married couples entered against one number in the same years. so the zadruga is not a smokvica peculiarity or a bunjevac one — it is how klenovica was organised too. houses 37, 38 and 59 hold a single child each and are something else, probably transient. one puzzle sits inside it. luka kalanj and kata miletic have children at house 22, then at 36 in 1892, then at 37 in 1894 — and two of them are called marija . whether that is a family moving twice in two years, a renumbering, or two entries for one child is not answerable from this file. four boys called antonius petrus and magdalena's children include an antonius born in 1865, another in 1868, a third in 1868 and a fourth in 1872. that is not an error. it is a necronym — a dead child's name given to the next born — and it is why the duplicate check has to read two death years as proof of two people rather than evidence of one. how they reach this archive not, as this page used to say, by marrying into the blazevic line — that is one marriage, lovro kalanj and klara blazevic. the chain that actually carries the family runs through hedviga's husband . ana kalanj , born at klenovica n° 22 on 3 january 1864 and baptised three days later, married josip de franceschi ; their son ante, their grandson pepe. every published kalanj is connected to hedviga by ordinary links — 100% , which only one other family here can say. what that means → four siblings, found loose in a photo library the baptisms of ana (1894), franciska (1896), zora (1898) and ivan (1900) — four consecutive children of martin kalanj and mornar — sailor . born rijeka , resident senj , roman catholic, born 1892, 1/iii — 1 march 1892. status: neoženjen , bachelor. bride milka vukelić , radnica u tvornici duhana — worker in the tobacco confidence. the point of saying so is that a reader can disagree with the reasoning instead of having to take the conclusion on trust. the five labels documented a named source with a reference, and where possible the scan. the strongest things in this archive are the familysearch citations into the croatian parish registers — senj, krivi put, otočac, karlobag — which give an image group, a page and a date. inferred a reasoned conclusion from documented facts, with the reasoning written out so it can be overturned. that the family is bunjevac is an inference from place and surname, not a statement in any record. superseded asserted in the family record, and now displaced by a document that says otherwise. disputed asserted in the family record but unsupported, or contradicted, by what can be seen — like the join at generation three . family lore told, remembered, not corroborated. kept because it is precious; labelled because pretending otherwise is how family myths become family history. both accounts of oto's death sit here. the rule that governs the whole build living people are not here they are not hidden, not gated, not present in the output. the rule is applied once, in classify_living() , at the boundary between the research data and the published site. because thousands of people in a tree this size carry no dates at all, judging each by their own record alone marks every one of them living — safe, but useless. so the build computes an upper bound on each person's birth year from their own events, their children's births, their marriages and their parents' bounds, and publishes somebody only when even the latest year they could have been born is more than a century ago. a recorded birth or christening → born in that year, exactly any recorded event in year e → born no later than e a child born in year c → born no later than c − 14 a marriage in year m → born no later than m − 14 a parent whose bound is p → born no later than p + 60 every step is a real bound, never a guess, and a recorded birth is never overridden by inference. on the current export that judges 2,034 of 15,643 people living. a living spouse, parent or child is not named on anybody else's page either. a removal request is honoured within days, without argument and without requiring a reason. this is stricter than its sister archives, and the difference is deliberate. the defranceschi archive publishes living people by name only — no dates, no places, no photographs , and the falco archive moved to the same rule in september 2026, naming 104 of them. this archive names none of its 2,034 . two reasons, and only one of them is principle. the scale is different — 2,034 living people against falco's 104 — and a rule that is comfortable for a hundred relatives is a different proposition for two thousand. and this archive is about one woman who died in 2001 : almost nothing it argues depends on anybody alive. where a living person is the only link in a chain, the page says “living, withheld” and the chain is shown broken rather than quietly completed. it is a divergence, not an oversight , and it is written here so that a reader moving between the family sites is not left wondering which rule is in force. an online family tree is a witness, not a source the spine here is a myheritage tree of 15,643 people . most “sources” attached to people in it are other trees — geni world family tree , boras web site , grlica web site , janicic , marko karic rodoslov . when four trees agree, that is four witnesses who may all have copied one another; it is not four documents. so the register page marks only whether a person carries any source string at all, and every person page prints the strings verbatim so a reader can see what kind of thing is being relied q: milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a   senj, 9 october 1886 — 7 september 1971 milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a factory. her life can be told almost entirely from records, and it is not the life the family tree describes. the tree carries milka lucia papić as the wife of ljubomir blažević and the mother of seven. the registers carry a woman who was married twice , widowed at twenty-eight , and spent more than forty years in the same tobacco factory — going in as a floor worker and coming out supervising it. senj baptisms, page 122, entry 96 born 9 october 1886 senj, roman catholic baptisms, str. 122 , entry 96. her entry is the second from the bottom of the left-hand page. name milka lucia — zakonita , legitimate born / baptised 9 october 1886 , baptised 17 october father josip papić , trhonoša — a load-carrier mother tonka rođ. prpić godparents josip glavičić , also a trhonoša , and ivka filipović baptised by the chaplain ( kapelan ) at senj later annotation the margin was written up again when she died — the register records the death entry and the date 7.9.1971 , endorsed at senj 30.9.1971 . a small correction. the family tree gives her baptism as 19 october . the register says 17 . the archive follows the register. both her father and her godfather are trhonoše — men who carried other people's goods on their backs for a fee. that is not a coincidence; it is a social world. in a port town whose port had died, the porters knew the porters . senj marriages, page 294, entry 30 first marriage, 4 november 1907 aged twenty-one, she married zvonimir m. vukelić — and nothing in the family tree's account of her had ever mentioned it. senj marriages, page 294, entry 30, boxed in red on the scan as held in the tree. date 4 studenoga (november) 1907 , senj groom zvonimir m. vukelić , gostioničarski pomoćnik — innkeeper's assistant . born 13 january 1883 . bachelor. bride milka papić , radnica u tvornici duhana — a worker in the tobacco factory. born 9 october 1886. unmarried. his parents petar vukelić , gostioničar — innkeeper, marked deceased — and vica her parents joso papić, gostioničar and tonka rođ. prpić witnesses kolomán pl. vukelić , a broker at the tobacco factory, and franjo olivieri , merchant banns married by episcopal dispensation , with the banns read once — on 3 november , the day before the wedding — instead of the usual three times her father has changed trade. in 1886 josip papić is a trhonoša . by 1907 the register calls him gostioničar — an innkeeper. the tree lists his occupations as “ trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar ”, and the two registers show that string is a sequence : the porter kept the money and bought a bar. the papići → the one-day dispensation is worth noticing without over-reading. her daughter miroslava was born in 1907 . a hurried wedding and a child in the same year is a familiar shape, but the register does not date the birth and this archive does not claim to know which came first. two children, and a widow at twenty-eight the vukelić children miroslava “mica” / “nana” vukelić (1907–1993), who married rahamin levi (1904–1984) of pirot ; and josip vukelić (1913–2004), born at senj. they are hedviga's half-brother and half-sister , and they were in the tree all along — invisible to the first build of this archive only because a sweep of somebody's ancestors never walks sideways. 1915 zvonimir vukelić died in 1915 , aged thirty-two, in the middle of the first world war. milka was twenty-eight , with a girl of eight and a boy of two. nothing in this archive says how he died, and 1915 is a year in which a man of thirty-two might die many ways. open questions → senj marriages, page 366, entry 41 second marriage, 8 december 1920 thirteen years after the first wedding and five years after the death, she married ljubomir blažević , a sailor. the register enters her under her married name: milka vukelić, udova — widow. she is still radnica u tvornici duhana . thirteen years on from her first marriage entry, the same job, the same words. the full entry → seven children followed, of whom hedviga was the fourth, born 3 august 1926 — and oto , who did not come home from the war. the factory, over a lifetime 1907, aged 21 radnica u tvornici duhana — worker , per the marriage register 1920, aged 34 radnica u tvornici duhana — still a worker , per the marriage register later supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory, per the family tree — at ul. stjepana radića 4 , “now a textile factory” and beside her anka blažević (1893–1953), her husband's sister, a radnica in the same factory this is the only career progression documented anywhere in this archive, and it belongs to a woman. in a town where the men are recorded as day labourers, porters and sailors, the steady wage was hers . why there was no other work → 7 september 1971 she died at senj, aged eighty-four, and is on the family stone as milka blažević rod. papić ✳ 1886 † 1971 — under her maiden name, not the vukelić name she carried into her second wedding, and beside the son whose body was never found. the grave → what is still missing. zvonimir vukelić's death entry for 1915, which would say how she was widowed; miroslava's 1907 birth entry, which would fix the order of wedding and child; and any record of what milka did between 1915 and 1920, alone with two children in a town with no work. twenty-two in the last year of the war. the family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot both be true, and there is no grave to ask. this page exists because the record contains a contradiction that has been kept rather than tidied away . both accounts are written into the same note on oto's entry, attributed to two different people, and this archive reproduces them exactly as they stand. the first account bitten by snake — attributed in the tree to ivan defranceski ivan anton defranceski (1925–1995) was hedviga's husband and oto's brother-in-law — two years younger than oto, and alive in the same town at the time. the velebit has the horned viper , vipera ammodytes , europe's most dangerous snake, and a shepherd or a labourer on that mountain was genuinely at risk. the second account the late otto blažević was the brother of ljuba, leo, aunt karma, aunt seka … he died in the war somewhere in slavonia , his grave is unknown, so they put his name in his grandmother's and grandfather's grave — and now leo is there, and katica. — attributed in the tree to nives blažević this one names his siblings correctly, including “aunt seka” — hedviga's own nickname — which is a good sign that the speaker knew the family well. what the second account fits the war in slavonia in 1945 is not a vague setting. it is one of the best-documented killing grounds of the european war's last months. the syrmian front ran from 21 october 1944 to 12 april 1945 across syrmia, slavonia and baranja. the yugoslav partisans lost more than 13,500 killed covering roughly 140 kilometres between belgrade and vinkovci over nearly six months of winter fighting. when the front broke on 12 april, the 1st and 3rd armies advanced west through slavonia . he had already seen the war close up. he was twenty when german aircraft destroyed about half of senj on 7–8 october 1943 , killing thirty of the town's residents — among them, on the second day, his uncle by marriage pavao kosina . a man born in 1923 was twenty-one or twenty-two in that campaign — precisely the cohort mobilised into it, much of it from newly-liberated croatia with minimal training. and an unknown grave is the ordinary outcome, not the strange one: thousands of those dead were buried where they fell. the detail that rings true. that the family cut his name into his grandparents' stone because there was no body is a specific, unglamorous, expensive act. people do it when someone does not come back from somewhere far away. it is much harder to explain if he died of a snakebite on the hill above the town. new evidence, september 2026 the grave says she was right about the grave a photograph of the blažević plot at senj — recovered from the myheritage media library, where it had been sitting untouched — can be checked against nives blažević's account line by line. it matches. ljubomir blažević ✳1891 †1966 · milka blažević rod. papić ✳1886 †1971 · oto blažević ✳1923 †1945 · mario blažević ✳1933 †1984 — and, on a later plaque, kata ✳1924 †2007 and leo ✳1920 †2008. she said “they put his name in … [the] grave” the stone oto blažević ✳ 1923 † 1945 is cut into it, between his mother and his brother mario. she said “and now leo is there, and katica ” the stone a separate, later, black plaque below reads leo ✳ 1920 † 2008 and kata ✳ 1924 † 2007 — katica. she said “his grandmother's and grandfather's grave” the stone the names are oto's parents . but nives blažević was born in 1953 — ljubomir and milka were her grandparents. she is describing the grave from where she stands in the family, which is what people do. what this does and does not settle. it does not show that oto died in slavonia. it shows that the witness who said so knew this grave in exact detail , including two burials added more than sixty years after his death — and that the family commemorated him on a stone rather than at a grave of his own, which is what you do for a man who does not come back. the
