q: papić porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront — and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the  senj and selce papić porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront — and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the town's cigarette factory. 116 published people 1742 earliest birth year 4 distinct spellings in the tree one change in four documents the tree lists josip “joso” papić's occupations as trhonoša, bremenar, gostioničar — load-carrier, porter, innkeeper — as though they were three trades in a row. four parish registers give him four words, and only one of them is a change. at his own wedding in 1885 he is a bremenar ; at his daughter milka's baptism in 1886 , a trhonoša ; at his daughter anica's in 1888 , a težak . those are not three trades — they are three words a priest reached for to mean a man who works with his body : burden-carrier, load-carrier, labourer. then at milka's wedding in 1907 he is a gostioničar . that is the change. he owns the inn. milka → the tobacco factory his daughter milka lucia papić (1886–1971) — hedviga's mother — was supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory in senj, an address the tree records as ul. stjepana radića 4 , “now a textile factory”. she was baptised at senj on 19 october 1886 , ten days after her birth, with josip glavičić and ivka filipović as godparents — one of the best-cited entries in this archive. a name changing in front of us the selce line is entered as “georgius juraj (joannis) papa ‘jure’ antić papić ” — carrying antić and papić at once — and seventy-nine people in this tree are written papić (papa) . the register settles that this is a real alternation and not a transcriber's slip: in the 1885 marriage entry the groom is josip papić and his father, on the very same line, is juraj papa . and the doubling is old: the 1806 baptismal entry for josephum at vinodol enters his mother as “matre marthe antich papa ” — both names on one line, eighty years before the tree's papić (papa) . his godfather is the village judge , judice mathia jellichich — of the family he would marry into. whether antić and papić were ever two families is now the open question. open questions → why the papići have no house number the blaževići can be traced through a single house number because the village registers of krmpote and krivi put record every child against one — smokvica 114 , krivi put 136 . the senj register does not. under mjesto obitavanja i kućni broj — place of residence and house number — the papić entries say simply “senj” , and nothing else. that is a difference between a town and a village, not between two families. it also means the zadruga that is visible at smokvica would be invisible here even if it existed , and no amount of reading senj baptisms will show it. the other half of this family hedviga's descent is not all peasants, and the other half arrives through this family. josip papić's mother was matija pilipić , and through her the line runs into karlobag , a free royal city on the coast under the velebit, and the register there speaks a different language about them: dominus at the 1768 baptism of places and four kinds of paper. each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stood in front of it with a phone — not because it would be nice to have. this archive has been built from a family tree, a media library and about thirty pages of parish register read on a screen. nobody involved in it has stood in any of these places. a phone is enough for all of it; none of this needs an appointment, and most of it needs no permission. photograph the whole thing and then the detail. a stone shot only close up cannot be placed in its row; a stone shot only wide cannot be read. and photograph the ones that look like nothing — a wrong house number is worth knowing too. go here first senj — the cemetery at sv. vid the blažević grave: ljubomir 1892–1966, milka 1886–1971, oto 1923–1945, mario 1933–1984. photograph the whole stone and each line close. tereza žubrinić's stone, 1867–1931, restored by the kosina family in 1991, with the wooden cross for vlč. antun kosina 1921–2003 standing against it. pavao and anka kosina's grave — his stone reads nevina žrtva zračnog napadaja na senj, an innocent victim of the air raid. why: toma blažević was buried here on 28 july 1907 and stanko papić on 4 june 1903. neither grave has been looked for. a cemetery register or a surviving stone would place them. smokvica krmpotska — house 114 the house itself, if it still stands, and the number if it is still on it. the neighbouring numbers, 112 and 116, so the run can be placed on the ground. anything carved or dated on the building. why: six documented years — 1838, 1882, 1884, 1888, 1890, 1895 — hold toma's children, pavao's children, jurko's children and two different men called ivo blažević. it is the zadruga the whole of question 1b turns on, and nobody in this archive has seen it. klenovica and povile — house 22 the house, if it stands, and the number on it — in both villages, because they may be the same building. whether klenovica 22 and povile 22 are one house, two houses, or one house the registers gave two village names. the kalanj graves in the klenovica cemetery beyond the one already photographed (lovro 1906–1965, ana 1919–1971, ivan 1942–1996, marijan 1944–2009). why: sixty-seven published people are entered at house 22 between 1840 and 1890 — the largest single household in this archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136. eleven couples have children recorded under both village names, which is why it is thought to be one house. nobody has stood in front of it. krivi put — house 136 the house, and 113 and 129 if the numbers survive. the church of the parish, and any war memorial. why: antonija perpić was born at 136 in 1859 into a household the register calls confiniarii. three prpić house numbers are known and none has been seen. when you are passing crikvenica — the hotel therapia the building, now the kvarner palace — the façade and, if they will let you in, the room that was the dining hall. any historic photograph the hotel keeps of its own interwar years. why: hedviga is remembered singing here. it is the only thing anyone has ever said about what she did, and the building is still standing — bought in 2013 and renamed. a photograph would turn a sentence of lore into something you can look at. senj — the tobacco factory the building on ul. stjepana radića 4, now a textile works. any plaque, date stone or surviving signage. why: milka supervised women rolling cigarettes here and antonija blažević held the same grade. across ten register pages between 1909 and 1919, most young women marrying in senj worked in it. if you get that far otočac and šumećica šumećica house 24, if the numbering survives. the parish church at otočac. prozor houses 50 and 245. why: the 1834 baptism puts a confiniarius household at šumećica 24. the žubrinići held five frontier offices out of these villages. karlobag the parish church. anything marking the town as a free royal city — the registers call it hujus civitatis. why: four generations of pilipići, urodas, smojvers and gerkacs, with a giustiniani standing godfather and a baron von holstein on the same page. the most socially distinct part of this descent. and anything on paper what why it matters here anything written on the back of a photograph studio stamps date and place a picture better than anything else here. fifteen photographs on /faces have no caption but a camera filename. letters, in any language nothing in this archive is in the family's own words. not one letter. identity papers, passports, work books a yugoslav passport application would date the emigration that question 1f cannot. funeral cards and death notices they carry the date, the parish and often the surviving relatives, all three. if you are holding a photograph and cannot say who is in it, that is worth as much — the contact sheet is fifteen pictures this archive cannot vouch for, and one conversation would close most of it. q: prpić bunjevci of the senj mountain, recorded for four generations at a single house number.  krivi put prpić bunjevci of the senj mountain, recorded for four generations at a single house number. antonija as entry 51: nata 12 may 1859 , baptisata 15 may , antonia perpić, legit. , daughter of the spouses joannes and lucia perpić , locus domicilii krivi put n⁰ 136 , godparents lucas tomljanović and anna tomljanović, daughter of andreas . house numbers are how frontier registers identify a family, and a settled household can hold one for a century. they were frontier households too the fuller of the two scans of antonija's 1859 baptism carries a conditio column the other crop omits, and the word in it is confiniar. — confiniarii . nor is it one household: on the same opening the perpić , tomljanović and butković families are all entered the same way. so krivi put was a military frontier village , exactly as otočac was. this archive had the bunjevac settlement and the žubrinić confiniarii as separate facts and never joined them. it came out of re-reading a document filed as a duplicate. the page proves the village read the other entries on the same opening and the bunjevac claim stops being an inference from place-names and becomes an observation. the surnames baptised at krivi put in the summer of 1859 are perpić, tomljanović, blažević, šojat, pavelić, vukelić, butković — and krmpotić , the clan the whole settlement is named for. every child is entered against a house number: n⁰ 4, 14, 15, 18, 23, 41, 51, 54, 58, 61, 72, 79, 81, 82, 136. prpić or perpić the tree writes it prpic 83 times, perpic 19, perpić 16, prpić 8 , once as perpich , and once — with admirable honesty — as “papić or perpic” . antonija is entered under both : “perpić / prpic”. this archive treats prpić and perpić as one name , which is a decision, and it is written down as one. where she is buried antonija died at senj on 2 february 1935 and is buried at mirogoj in zagreb — the monumental cemetery, a long way from krivi put. nothing in the record explains why, and it is worth explaining. open questions → where they were born 26 krivi put 136, senj, lika-senj county, croatia daughter of andreas . house numbers are how frontier registers identify a family, and a settled household can hold one for a century. they were frontier households too the fuller of the two scans of antonija's 1859 baptism carries a conditio column the other crop omits, and the word in it is confiniar. — confiniarii . nor is it one household: on the same opening the perpic , tomljanovic and butkovic families are all entered the same way. so krivi put was a military frontier village , exactly as otocac was. this archive had the bunjevac settlement and the zubrinic confiniarii as separate facts and never joined them. it came out of re-reading a document filed as a duplicate. the page proves the village read the other entries on the same opening and the bunjevac claim stops being an inference from place-names and becomes an observation. the surnames baptised at krivi put in the summer of 1859 are perpic, tomljanovic, blazevic, sojat, pavelic, vukelic, butkovic — and krmpotic , in the strict sense that two-thirds of the published people reach hedviga only through a sorting label. read this before you read the list entries marked family tree are the 1,297 people this archive publishes from the family's myheritage tree. they are what the family believes , not what a record proves — and this archive has now shown several of them to be wrong, including a man attached to his own grandson's generation . treat each as a claim until it appears on this page a second time with a register beside it. what cannot be true → entries marked read in the register are people met while reading the parish books act by act — godparents, witnesses, the officiating priest, the parents of the person marrying in, and the other brides on the page . a baptism names a priest and two godparents; a marriage names four parents, two witnesses and an officiant. almost none of them are kin. they are here because they were found, not because they are family , and they are the part of the record a pedigree throws away. nothing here is invented. where the register gives a trade, a rank or a house number it is recorded in the register's own words — nadglednica u tvornici duhana , q: rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 19  santou isaac codron, 1913–1997 rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 1944 — and he died in south africa in 1997. how he came to be alive to marry her is the most interesting unanswered question in this archive. the tree records him plainly and briefly: santou (shemtov) isaac codron , born 13 september 1913 at rhodes , died 16 april 1997 in south africa of cardio-respiratory arrest, married to hedviga about 1973 . that is every fact held on him. each one opens onto a large history. shemtov — shem tov , “good name” — is a sephardic given name, and codron is a known rhodes jewish surname. he was, on the face of the record, a rhodesli . 23 july 1944 what happened to the community he was born into rhodes held a sephardic jewish community that had been there since the fifteenth century, speaking judeo-spanish — the language their ancestors carried out of spain in 1492. in the quarter called la djuderia it was still, in 1944, a living world. on 20 july 1944 the ss ordered the island's jews to assemble for a document check. 1,615 people from rhodes , together with 94 from kos , were packed into the cargo holds of livestock ships, taken to the greek mainland, and put on a train. they arrived at auschwitz on 16 august 1944 after what is generally called the longest deportation journey of the holocaust . about 1,200 were murdered on arrival. roughly 150 survived. santou codron was thirty in july 1944. if he was on rhodes that month, he was almost certainly on that transport — and the odds of walking out of it were about one in eleven. the likelier explanation, and why he probably was not there — because the rhodes jews had been leaving for southern africa for fifty years, and that is exactly where he turns up. rhodesli men began going to africa for work at the end of the nineteenth century; mousa and solomon benatar settled in southern rhodesia in 1895 . emigration accelerated through the 1920s and 1930s, to the belgian congo , southern rhodesia and south africa — for economic reasons first, and from 1938 because of the italian racial laws, rhodes then being italian territory. sephardim from rhodes settled in salisbury , today's harare, and founded a synagogue there in 1932 . in all, close to two thousand jews from rhodes lived in the congo and southern rhodesia between the 1920s and the 1960s. now set hedviga's own movements beside that. she came to south africa from zimbabwe — that is, from rhodesia — in april 1975 , and she is recorded as marrying codron around 1973 , which places the marriage in the rhodesian years. so the meeting has an obvious setting. a croatian woman from senj and a sephardic jew from rhodes, both a long way from home, in the small european society of late-colonial rhodesia — a community he most likely belonged to because his family had been part of that specific migration for decades before the war. this is an inference, not a document. what this archive does and does not claim documented born 13 september 1913, rhodes. died 16 april 1997, south africa, of cardio-respiratory arrest. married hedviga blažević c. 1973. inferred that he was a rhodes sephardi — from the given name shemtov , the surname codron and the birthplace together. inferred that he most likely reached southern africa before the war, as part of the documented rhodes-to-rhodesia migration — because he was alive in 1973 and because that route was well travelled. not claimed that he survived auschwitz. nothing in this record says he was deported, and treating him as a survivor because he was born in the right place at the right time would be an invention. it would also be a serious one. not claimed that his family escaped. the codron name appears among rhodes jewish families; who among them was deported in july 1944 has not been checked here against the yad vashem or rhodes jewish museum registers. what would settle it. south african immigration and naturalisation papers would give his arrival year and last residence outright. the rhodes jewish museum and yad vashem hold community and deportation registers in which a codron born 13 september 1913 would either appear or be the dates do. what happened italy capitulated on 8 september 1943 , and the italian occupation zone along the adriatic collapsed. senj, with its harbour and its road up to lika, became one of the most important partisan ports on the coast: weapons and war material were concentrated in the town and ships lay in the harbour. on 7 and 8 october 1943 german aircraft bombed the town and the port. 52 killed — 30 local residents and 22 foreigners ~60 civilians recorded seriously or lightly wounded 50% of the town destroyed to its foundations; only about a quarter of buildings still habitable figures from the croatian scholarly literature on the german bombing of senj in 1943. sources → the family in it anka blažević's household anka blažević (1893–1953) was ljubomir's sister — hedviga's aunt, and the radnica who worked the floor of the tobacco factory alongside her sister-in-law milka . on 20 november 1919 she married pavao kosina , born at senj on 15 march 1894. pavao kosina b. 15 march 1894, senj — died 8 october 1943 , the second day of the bombing otilija kosina b. 1920 — died 1943 , no day recorded antun kosina b. 1921 — died 2003. a priest : his cross reads vlč. — velečasni , reverend oskar kosina b. 4 september 1922, senj — died 1954, buenos aires neda kosina b. 1924 — died 7 september 1943 , a month before the raid križan kosina b. 1940 — died 1941, an infant anka outlived them by a decade and died in 1953. confirmed, september 2026 — an inference becomes a document the stone says it outright this page first said pavao kosina was probably one of the thirty, and was careful to add that the date came from the family tree rather than from any record. then his grave was found in the media library. the kosina plot, senj. three portrait medallions below the inscription. ovdje počiva u miru božjem pavao kosina ✳ 15.iii.1894. · pog. 8.x.1943. nevina žrtva zračnog napadaja na senj u znak sjećanja podiže — zahvalna supruga i sinovi “here rests in god's peace pavao kosina, born 15 march 1894, killed 8 october 1943. an innocent victim of the air raid on senj. raised in memory by his grateful wife and sons.” pog. is poginuo — killed, the word used for a violent death rather than an ordinary one. the family did not merely record the date; s: Senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. Every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sai
q: senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sai  the town the railway went around senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sailor, cigarette-factory hand — is a consequence of one decision taken in 1873. senj sits under the velebit at the head of the senjska draga , where the bura comes off the mountain hard enough to stop traffic. it is one of the oldest towns on the croatian coast, and for four hundred years it was a place of consequence: a free royal town, a bishopric, a habsburg military port, and the home of the uskoks . 1537–1618 the uskoks and nehaj when the ottomans took klis in 1537, its defenders — refugees the slavs called uskoci , “the ones who jumped in” — fell back to senj. the habsburgs put them on the frontier payroll and let them raid. they became, depending on who was writing, a christian bulwark or a pirate confederacy; in practice both, because vienna paid them irregularly and they took the difference out of venetian and ottoman shipping. in 1558 the captain ivan lenković built nehaj on the hill above the town, using stone from the churches and monasteries outside the walls so that a besieger would have nothing to shelter behind. it was the uskok headquarters until the uskok war of 1615–18 ended with venice and vienna agreeing to disperse them inland. nehaj still stands over the town, and it is the thing everyone photographs. this archive claims no uskok descent. the uskoks were broken up in 1618 and the earliest person in this tree is born about 1717 — a century later. what the uskok period explains is not the family's blood but the family's place : it is why there was a fortified, garrisoned, habsburg-administered town here at all, and why the empty mountain behind it was about to be settled on purpose. the settlement → the turning point 1873: the railway goes to rijeka senj's whole nineteenth century was built on being the port where the lika highlands met the sea. timber, wool and livestock came down the roads from the interior and went out through senj. then the karlovac–rijeka railway opened in 1873 and did not come here. the traffic followed the rails to rijeka. senj's port trade collapsed, and it never recovered. this is the single most important economic fact in this archive, because the family's recorded work sits directly downstream of it: toma blažević 1838–1907 nadničar — day labourer. born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska ; died at senj and buried there. a man who came off the mountain to a town that had no work left. josip “joso” papić 1857–1939 trhonoša, bremenar, gostioničar — load-carrier, porter, innkeeper. the first two are the same job twice: carrying other people's goods on your back for a fee. the third is what he made of it. ljubomir blažević 1892–1966 mornar — sailor. born at rijeka , not senj — the family had already followed the work to the port that got the railway. he came back, and died at senj. milka papić 1886–1971 supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory , tvornica duhana , senj. her sister-in-law anka blažević (1893–1953) was a radnica — a floor worker — at the same factory. the tobacco factory the habsburg tobacco monopoly was extended to croatia, slavonia and the military frontier by an imperial patent of 20 november 1850 , effective from march 1851, and state tobacco factories followed across the region. senj's was one of them, and for two generations of this family it was the employer of last resort in a town with no port trade — women's work, indoors, waged, and steady in a way that carrying sacks was not. after the second world war the senj factory was liquidated and its cigarette-making machinery was transferred to the tobacco factory at rovinj . the tree records the building's later life exactly: the address is given as ul. stjepana radića 4, 53270 senj , with the note that it “now is a textile factory”. and it is why these families met. one page of the senj marriage register for 1918 carries three brides entered as radnica u tvornici duhana — from otočac/šumećica , from krivi put , and from senj . those are the three places this archive comes from. counting milka , her sister-in-law anka , antonija blažević and ana papić , six women of these families worked that floor. the factory was the institution that brought the mountain villages into the town — and it is a large part of why a blažević of smokvica, a prpić of krivi put and a žubrinić of otočac end up in one family. unverified here. the senj factory's founding date, size and closure year have not been confirmed from a croatian source by this archive. the monopoly patent and the transfer of machinery to rovinj are documented generally; the specific history of the senj plant is an open question . two days that finished what the railway started 7–8 october 1943 after italy's capitulation senj became one of the most important partisan ports on the adriatic, and german aircraft bombed the town and harbour over two days in october 1943. thirty local residents were killed and about half the town was destroyed to its foundations ; only a quarter of the buildings were still habitable. hedviga was seventeen. her aunt's husband died on the second day. senj, 1943 → and then the boats out a port town with no port sends its people away. this tree records the destinations plainly: port pirie in south australia , where ivan žubrinić went about 1884 and where his descendants feed it. every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sailor, cigarette-factory hand — is a consequence of one decision taken in 1873. senj sits under the velebit at the head of the senjska draga , where the bura comes off the mountain hard enough to stop traffic. it is one of the oldest towns on the croatian coast, and for four hundred years it was a place of consequence: a free royal town, a bishopric, a habsburg military port, and the home of the uskoks . 1537–1618 the uskoks and nehaj when the ottomans took klis in 1537, its defenders — refugees the slavs called uskoci , “the ones who jumped in” — fell back to senj. the habsburgs put them on the frontier payroll and let them raid. they became, depending on who was writing, a christian bulwark or a pirate confederacy; in practice both, because vienna paid them irregularly and they took the difference out of venetian and ottoman shipping. in 1558 the captain ivan lenkovic built nehaj on the hill above the town, using stone from the churches and monasteries outside the walls so that a besieger would have nothing to shelter behind. it was the uskok headquarters until the uskok war of 1615–18 ended with venice and vienna agreeing to disperse them inland. nehaj still stands over the town, and it is the thing everyone photographs. this archive claims no uskok descent. the uskoks were broken up in 1618 and the earliest person in this tree is born about 1717 — a century later. what the uskok period explains is not the family's blood but the family's place : it is why there was a fortified, garrisoned, habsburg-administered town here at all, and why the empty mountain behind it was about to be settled on purpose. the settlement → the turning point 1873: the railway goes to rijeka senj's whole nineteenth century was built on being the port where the lika highlands met the sea. timber, wool and livestock came down the roads from the interior and went out through senj. then the fact in this archive, because the family's recorded work sits directly downstream of it: toma blazevic 1838–1907 nadnicar — day labourer. born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska ; died at senj and buried there. a man who came off the mountain to a town that had no work left. josip “joso” papic 1857–1939 trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar — load-carrier, porter, innkeeper. the first two are the same job twice: carrying other people's goods on your back for a fee. the third is what he made of it. ljubomir blazevic 1892–1966 mornar — sailor. born at rijeka , not senj — the family had already followed the work to the port that got the railway. he came back, and died at senj. milka papic 1886–1971 supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory , tvornica duhana , senj. her sister-in-law anka blazevic (1893–1953) was a radnica — a floor worker — at the same factory. the tobacco factory the habsburg tobacco monopoly was extended to croatia, slavonia and the military frontier by an imperial patent of 20 november 1850 , effective from march 1851, and state tobacco factories followed across the region. senj's was one of them, and for two generations of this family it was the employer of last resort in a town with no port trade — women's work, indoors, waged, and steady in a way that carrying sacks was not. after the second world war the senj factory was liquidated and its cigarette-making machinery was transferred to the tobacco factory at rovinj . the tree records the building's later life exactly: the address is given as ul. stjepana radica 4, 53270 senj , with the note that it “now is a textile factory”. and it is why these families met. one page of the senj marriage register for 1918 carries three brides entered as radnica u tvornici duhana — from otocac/sumecica , from krivi put , and from senj . those are the three places this archive comes from. counting milka , her sister-in-law anka , antonija blazevic and ana papic , six women of these of otocac end up in one family. unverified here. the senj factory's founding date, size and closure year have not been confirmed from a croatian source by this archive. the monopoly patent and the what they did the family tree records a trade for sixteen people out of twelve hundred. the registers record one for almost everybody, in a column this archive had been reading past. both the latin and the croatian parish forms carry a conditio or stalež column, and the priest filled it in — for the parents, for the godparents, and for the witnesses. it is the only place in these documents where a person is described by something other than their name and their kin. this archive had been reading past it. where an occupation surfaced it went into prose on one person's page and nowhere else, which meant it could not be counted or compared. the comparison is the point. two families, two worlds, twenty miles apart the žubrinići hold offices confiniarius — a man of the military frontier , šumećica n° 24, 1834 confiniarius ex pago dubrava n° 29 — and so is marcus orešković , whose daughter married into this line. both sides of that marriage are frontier households. vigiliarum magister pensionatus — master of the watch, pensioned silvarum custos — forest warden, šumećica custos carcerum — keeper of the prison, otočac, 1845 forest ranger — otočac, the 1837 generation kontrolor gradske daće — municipal excise controller, senj, 1910 six salaried posts, four of them in a single parish register, three of them in one entry . these are people the state paid. the blaževići carry things nadničar — day labourer. toma blažević, senj, at his death in 1907 seljaci — peasants. toma and tereza at smokvica 114, 1884 selj. — the same, jurko and tereza, 1895 težak — labourer. josip papić, senj, 1891 trhonoša, bremenar, gostioničar — porter, burden-carrier, innkeeper no office, no pension, no rank. the papići carry sacks in the port; the blaževići work by the day. these families are twenty miles apart and they married each other. hedviga descends from both — from a household that held the keys to the otočac gaol and from a household whose head was entered, at his death, as a man who worked by the day. the frontier → added 13 september 2026 the offices did not travel australian electoral rolls give an occupation and a street address for every adult, every roll year, from 1913. for the branch that went to port pirie that turns a family this archive knew only by name into a family it knows by trade — and the answer is not what the croatian record would lead you to expect. who occupation where year arthur leslie zubrinich ironmoulder 2 daisy st, port pirie east 1941, 1943 keith leo zubrinich moulder 9 queen street, port pirie 1939 edward malcolm zubrinich labourer 65 queen street, solomontown 1939 maurice joseph zubrinich labourer 56 simpson road, port pirie 1939 john stephen zubrinich labourer whyalla 1939 john william zubrinich labourer wolfram street, broken hill 1913 catherine zubrinich domestic duties wolfram street, broken hill 1913 austa louise zubrinich domestic duties 21 st ann's terrace, glenelg 1939 in lika these people held offices — warden of the forest, master of the watch, keeper of the prison, and a rank the register writes as confiniarius . at port pirie, two generations later, they are labourers and moulders in a lead smelter . the offices did not travel. what a frontier household held was a position in a system, and the system did not exist in south australia — so the family arrived as what the smelter needed. the one man who climbed is arthur leslie, an ironmoulder , which is a skilled trade and not a labouring one. two small things the addresses give away. edward malcolm at 65 queen street and keith leo at 9 queen street are on the same street in 1939, and solomontown is where their father died. and john william and catherine are at the same broken hill address in 1913 — a mining town four hundred kilometres inland, which is where the family went before port pirie held them. read off the registers each row cites the entry it came from. nothing here is inferred, and where a word is ambiguous it q: the žubrinić fragments this archive has said for months that joining the žubrinići is the largest piece of work left in it. counting it properl  422 records, 397 real people, 115 loose ends the žubrinić fragments this archive has said for months that joining the žubrinići is the largest piece of work left in it. counting it properly says something worse and more useful: 81 of the 115 loose ends are bare names with neither a date nor a place, and exactly one pair can be joined from what the tree holds. corrected: two numbers this archive published were both wrong the site has been saying “232 records resolving into 94 separate root ancestors” . neither figure survives checking. 232 was too low. the surname fold split on a bracket but not on a slash, so žubrinić / xubrinich and žubrinić zubrinic xubrinich — one surname written several ways in one field — never matched the surname list at all. the real figure is 422 . fixing it brought 214 people into this archive who had been sitting outside it, among them elias ilija žubrinić and casparus žubrinić — the subjects of two of this archive's own open questions . 94 was the right shape for the wrong reason. the true count is 115 , and it is high because of something the old number never named — see below. ninety-two people hang off an alphabet the tree contains 18 nodes whose entire given name is a single letter — m , j , t — each with a parent called “žubrinić zubrinix xubrinic zub” , and each holding as children the žubrinići whose names begin with that letter. one of them has 26 children ; another has 17. that is a filing system, not a family. between them these eighteen nodes hold 92 people . counted as parentage — which is what a naive read does — the žubrinići look joined. they are not: those 92 people are attached to the letter their name starts with and to nothing else. this archive's own sorting-bucket filter did not catch them, because a bucket is normally detected by words like “to be sorted” and these are named a through w . what is actually left, and what can be done with it state how many what it means anchored 7 a year and a place. these are the only ones a register search can start from. dated 26 a year and no place. searchable only if you already know the parish. placed 1 a place and no year. a century of register to read. bare 81 neither. a name and a surname. nothing in this archive will ever move them, and no amount of work on the tree will either. so the honest answer to “can the žubrinići be joined?” is no — not from here. 81 of 115 have nothing to search on. the joining has to come out of the otočac registers , and this archive has read two pages of them. the 4 pairs the tree can offer gregorius gregory žubrinić zubrinic xubrinich 1785 antonius žubrinić not people. they are labels somebody typed into the father's slot while sorting, and this archive already found four of them being published as ancestors and removed them — from the list of people . nobody removed them from the list of parents . so a žubrinić whose only father is the phrase “brothers of josephus” was counted by this page as joined . across the whole archive, 21 sorting buckets
